answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with slow trust aging: a new identity earns only a tiny capped share, and its cap rises layer by layer, like a pearl forming, only after consecutive epochs of distinct verified work. A farm crossing this tundra must keep thousands of fakes alive and working for many epochs, paying upkeep every epoch for almost nothing. Its newborns mirror each other in age and history, so the cluster is visible, while one honest agent simply ages once doing work it already does.
